description: Threat-to-accountability crosswalk for the CoSAI AI Shared Responsibility Framework. Maps each named AI security threat to the SRF layer where it lands and the accountable persona per operating model. The SRF does not define threats, attack techniques, or severity. Every threat definition here belongs to its external source. This file adds who must authorize the mitigating activity, who owns each finding, and who signs the residual risk. Threat catalogs do not carry those answers. obligations[] is a risk-to-obligation link. A derived_via_control link is stored only when a related control's citation matches a current obligation. That basis means the link was reached through the control, and the source lists the control id and the citation. basis official_text means the cited provision's wording covers the risk. The source then names the URL, the article and paragraph, and a short excerpt. A named_citation link is derived. The requirement states a duty that addresses the risk. The text does not state the harm, and the link does not run through a control. No link is stored without one of those bases. Eleven draft L1 rows and nineteen draft L2 and L3 rows add business, information, and application risks. Fifteen draft L4 and L5 rows add platform and AI Model Provider risks. L1-tagged requirements that state one of those risks are linked on the row. Their definitions are cited to the MIT AI Risk Repository and to OECD/LEGAL/0449 and the OECD AI Incidents Monitor. The draft rows are for review and are not a claim that the catalog is closed.
id_convention: AI Exchange entries are keyed by the OWASP AI Exchange permalink slug (the stable identifier in owaspai.org/go/<slug>/ URLs). Entries that exist only in the OWASP GenAI Data Security Risks taxonomy are keyed dsgaiNN (lowercase), matching the published DSGAI identifier. Threat names for AI Exchange rows are taken verbatim from the AI Exchange AI security matrix; names for DSGAI-only rows are taken verbatim from the DSGAI 2026 taxonomy. impact and attack_surface for DSGAI-only rows are derived from the published DSGAI summary, because that taxonomy does not use the AI Exchange field names. Mappings reference external IDs exactly as published by each source; a null mapping means no defensible one-to-one mapping exists, not that none was looked for. This file cites DSGAI identifiers; it does not copy DSGAI mitigation text. Control references use canonical srf.control.<vertical>.<control-id> IDs from /ids.json. DSGAI07 (governance, lifecycle, and classification as an enabling condition) and DSGAI08 (regulatory non-compliance as an outcome) have no rows: they are not attack techniques. Classification and provenance duties already sit on the Data Provider persona at L2. Draft L1 business and usage rows are keyed by a short slug (overreliance, outofpurpose, inventorygap, missingoversight, ailititeracy, unclearaccountability, misleadingclaims, highriskuse, noimpactassessment, uncontestable, unreportedincidents). Draft L4 and L5 rows add slugs such as weakplatformmfa, incompleteplatformqms, unscreenedmodelpersonnel, and opaquefederalmodelacq. Draft L2 and L3 rows add slugs such as incompletetechdoc, missinginforecords, nopremarketconformity, and unlabeledsyntheticout. Draft L4 and L5 rows add slugs such as weakplatformmfa, incompleteplatformqms, unscreenedmodelpersonnel, and opaquefederalmodelacq. Those slugs are not external catalog ids. Their names are SRF labels for the sourced risk. The MIT and OECD fields cite the published taxonomy labels and the retrieved monitor pages.
accountability_convention: One accountable persona per threat per operating model. The responsibility object quotes the customer and provider cell values verbatim from /data/matrix.json for the threat's primary SRF layer. Where the matrix says shared, this file still names a single accountable lead and records the counterparty obligation in the note, because shared is not a valid final answer.

verification.method: AI Exchange slugs and matrix rows verified against owaspai.org (AI security matrix, permalink set). ATLAS technique IDs verified against atlas.mitre.org technique pages and the MISP galaxy mirror of ATLAS attack patterns. LLM Top 10 2025 IDs verified against genai.owasp.org. BIML IDs verified against the BIML-LLM24 report text, which uses the bracket convention [LLMtop10:n:name]. DSGAI identifiers and names verified against the OWASP GenAI Data Security Risks & Mitigations 2026 taxonomy (DSGAI01 to DSGAI21) as published at genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-genai-data-security-risks-mitigations-2026/ and in datasets/_shared/dsgai_taxonomy.json of the OWASP GenAI Data Security Initiative repository. New DSGAI-only rows use only ATLAS and LLM IDs already present in this file or on the 2025 LLM Top 10 list; invented IDs are not used.
verification.policy: TBD or null is acceptable; invented IDs are not.
